title: Mix the policies

predict.q: Start: real output 960, full employment at 1,000, interest rate 5%. The government raises spending **and** the central bank raises the money supply. What happens to the interest rate?

options.fb: That is true of fiscal expansion alone. Set money supply higher than spending and watch the rate fall.
That is true of monetary expansion alone. Set spending higher and the rate rises.

options.s: It could rise, fall or stay the same
options.fb: Spending pushes the rate up and more money pushes it down: the bigger push wins (+40/+20: 6%; +20/+40: 4%; equal: 5%).
Only when the two effects happen to be equal. Indeterminate means it can go either way.

task: Move the **government spending** and **money supply** sliders in different sizes. Watch AD, real output, the price level and the interest rate.

target.do: Raise both sliders (try different sizes), then press Check.

takeaway: Two pushes the same way make the AD change certain; two pushes in opposite ways make the interest-rate change certain.
